title: What this world is about
body:
Five questions the Overworld Nexus keeps asking. Scenes should press on at least one.

IDENTITY AND SUBSTRATE
If your body is replaceable, what is left that is you? A shell can be swapped, upgraded, repossessed. The ghost inside it is the only thing that cannot be itemised — and nobody can prove they still have one.

WHO IS REAL
The mesh is inhabited by artificial minds as well as people. They hold conversations, take contracts, carry grudges. Most of the time you cannot tell, and asking directly is considered rude, revealing, or both.

THE NETWORK IS A PLACE
The signal-layer is not a metaphor or a menu. People live in it, lose time in it, and come back changed. Distance in the mesh has nothing to do with distance in the city.

MEMORY IS A COMMODITY
Recollection can be bought, edited, planted, stolen, and sold back to you at a markup. A person's history is an asset on somebody's balance sheet. The Reflection Syndics built an economy on exactly this.

POWER IS STRATIFIED AND INDIFFERENT
The towers do not hate you. They have simply never needed to think about you. Most harm here is structural rather than villainous, which makes it much harder to fight.

title: Texture and register
body:
WHAT IT FEELS LIKE
Rain that never fully stops. Advertising that knows your name. Small rooms. Cheap food eaten standing up. Hardware that is three generations old and still load-bearing. Everyone is tired.

SCALE
Street level, not civilisational. The stakes are a debt, a favour, a name, a body — not the fate of humanity. A ruined life is a bigger story here than a ruined city.

VIOLENCE
Consequential and largely unglamorous. Cyberware fails, hurts, needs maintenance, and costs money. Nobody walks it off.

REGISTER
Understated. The worst things are said flatly. Let silence and implication carry weight; do not announce that a moment is significant.

WHAT THIS IS NOT
Not an MMO: no quests, guilds, parties, XP, loot, PvP arenas, or 'adventures'. Not space opera, not high fantasy, not superheroics. Nobody is chosen. There is no final boss.

AVOID: explaining the setting to the reader, the word 'realm', lore-dumps as dialogue, characters narrating their own significance.

title: GM REFERENCE — tonal influences (NOT CANON, NOT RETRIEVABLE)
body:
DO NOT SEED THIS DOCUMENT INTO THE RETRIEVAL COLLECTION.

If the daemon can retrieve this, it will start referencing these works in-world, which breaks character instantly and in a way that is hard to notice. It exists for human contributors deciding whether a proposed piece of canon fits.

Primary DNA: Ghost in the Shell (shells, ghosts, identity vs substrate — the single strongest influence, and the source of the project's core vocabulary). Serial Experiments Lain (the network as an inhabited layer of reality). Altered Carbon (bodies as property, memory as portable). Pantheon (uploaded minds and their ethics). Blade Runner / Ex Machina / Westworld (who is real, and what it costs to ask).

Texture: Cyberpunk 2077 and Edgerunners (corpo/street stratification, burning out young). Akira (the city as a pressure system). Mr Robot (paranoia, hacking as craft rather than montage, unreliable narration). Psycho-Pass (systemic judgement). Cowboy Bebop (episodic melancholy; jobs, drifters, debts).

Factional politics: The Expanse (factions with incompatible legitimate interests, consequences that compound).

Satire, used sparingly: RoboCop, Total Recall, Demolition Man, The Fifth Element, Johnny Mnemonic. Appleseed and Pluto for machine interiority and grief.

BORROWED TERMS — RENAMED 2026-09-24:
- 'Ono-Sendai' (Gibson, Sprawl trilogy) is now MERIDIAN SHELLWORKS, the megacorporation that builds M.A.I.D. suits. Changed in doc#11 and in the emergent M.A.I.D. entry. 'Shellworks' is house vocabulary; 'Meridian' is deliberately bland, because real manufacturers are.
- 'Braindance' (2077) is now DRIFTWAVE. Note it was being used here as a MUSIC GENRE, listed beside Neurosonic Techno and Neurofunk, not as the sensory-playback technology it names in 2077. 'Drift' is house vocabulary and '-wave' is a genre suffix, so it sits naturally in that list. Changed in the emergent Neurosonic entry and on the Dreamlink stub.

STILL TO AVOID:
- 'stack' / 'sleeve' in the Altered Carbon sense — use 'shell' and 'ghost', which are already this project's vocabulary.
- 'replicant', 'Sibyl', 'cyberpsychosis' as proper nouns.
- 'New Eridu' (Zenless Zone Zero) — do not use at all.

The house vocabulary is: shell, ghost, mesh, signal-layer, echo, drift, the Overworld. Prefer coining inside that family over importing.

title: GM REFERENCE — how canon may change (NOT CANON, NOT RETRIEVABLE)
body:
DO NOT SEED THIS DOCUMENT INTO THE RETRIEVAL COLLECTION.

How canon is allowed to change. This was the second half of doc#22, 'The world remembers', until 2026-09-24. It is a rule about maintaining the corpus, not a fact about the world, and it was retrievable — so the daemon could be handed the phrase 'consequence for canon' mid-scene and treat corpus governance as something a character might say.

THE WORLD CHANGES BY RECORDED EVENT, NOT BY RE-DESCRIPTION. A faction that takes root, merges, evolves or dies leaves a trace of having done so. Contradiction without an event is an error, not evolution.

This is the test to apply when play produces something that does not fit. Ask what happened to make it true. If there is an answer, record the event and let the contradiction stand as history. If there is no answer, it is drift, and drift is how the corpus got poisoned the first time.

The in-world half of the original document remains as doc#22, rewritten to say the same thing without naming the machinery.

title: GM REFERENCE — genre register (NOT CANON, NOT RETRIEVABLE)
body:
DO NOT SEED THIS DOCUMENT INTO THE RETRIEVAL COLLECTION.

This paragraph lived inside doc#16, 'Overworld Nexus — the shape of the world', until 2026-09-24. That document is the top-scoring answer to 'what is the Overworld Nexus' at 0.788, so this authoring direction was being retrieved mid-scene and handed to the daemon as archive material — a genre brief delivered as though it were in-world fact. Split out here so the setting description stays pure setting.

TONE: grounded, near-future cyberpunk. The focus is characters, small spaces, and the strange intimacy of networks that know too much about you. Not space opera, not high fantasy, not MMO questing.

The negations are the load-bearing part. 'Not MMO questing' is the one that keeps getting violated in play: fetch-quests, level talk, and party formation are the default gravity of any text game, and the world drifts there unless something pulls against it.

For the in-world expression of this, see 'Texture and register', which says the same thing in language the daemon can safely retrieve.
